transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump is now on his way to China after expressing appreciation for his hosts in the Philippines.
I very much appreciate your welcoming me and us back to the Philippines as we reaffirm one of America's oldest and most important alliances in the Pacific.
During a state luncheon at the Philippine presidential palace, Trump said he has concluded what he calls a very big trade deal with the Philippines.
Trump said it's a fair deal for both countries, but he did not provide any details, and there's been no comment from the Philippine president.
Waiting for him in China is his highly anticipated meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Former Congresswoman Mary Peltola is returning to Washington this time as a senator from Alaska.
She is unseated incumbent Dan Sullivan.
According to a race call by the Associated Press, it's the latest Republican-held seat seized by Democrats this election cycle.
And here's Eric McDaniel reports.
Peltola ran a campaign squarely centered on Alaskan issues, fish, family, and freedom.
The moderate Democrat previously served in Congress as Alaska's sole House member.
Her Senate race was a controversial one.
The New York Times spoke to a former campaign staffer who alleged Democrats recruited a man with the same name as her opponent into the race.
She denies involvement, and NPR has not independently confirmed the allegations.
Peltola's race is the final Senate race to be called.
Democrats will control the chamber 56 to 44.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News in Washington.
Democrats are also celebrating a victory in North Carolina where Raymond Smith has defeated Republican Congressman Greg Murphy in a tight House race.
Former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before Congress,
and PR Shannon Bond reports on the scrutiny he'll face over national security scandals swirling around the company.
Jensen Huang and NVIDIA's top lawyer will answer questions from the House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence Committees
and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party in early December.
The interviews will take place behind closed doors.
Lawmakers say they want answers about NVIDIA's role in alleged chip smuggling
and efforts to evade export controls meant to block China from accessing the most advanced U.S. chips.
And they'll ask Huang about his involvement with a woman U.S. intelligence officials say was recruited by China's top spy agency.
NPR has not independently confirmed those reports.
Shannon Bond, NPR News.
NVIDIA has rejected Jensen Huang's offer to return as the company's chief executive.
NVIDIA chairman Harvey Jones said at the start of a quarterly earnings call Tuesday
that the company's board had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and does not intend to reinstate him.
You're listening to NPR News.
The end of the two-month criminal trial of China's Huawei Technologies is near a jury in Brooklyn,
likely to begin deliberations later today after two days of closing arguments.
Prosecutors call Huawei a criminal enterprise that helped Iran spy on its citizens and steal from U.S. companies.
The defense says prosecutors have been spinning a false narrative.
Massive waves reaching above 30 feet and fueled by a strong El Nino have been pounding the California coast over the past week.
From member station KQED, Ezra David Romero reports on more of these monster waves, which are on the way.
In Pacifica, south of San Francisco, the powerful waves crashed into the back of Lou Rabin's weathered red home,
which sits just a few feet from the Pacific Ocean.
He was out of town when the waves hit, and he was relieved to find his house still standing when he returned.
There's some minor things. All in all, it's held up 99 percent.
I've been very lucky that the house is still here.
The large waves are expected to churn up the coastline again later this week as a series of storms hits the region.
Climate scientists are worried a storm, big waves, higher seas, and king tides could create major flooding around Thanksgiving.
For NPR News, I'm Ezra David Romero in San Francisco.
The financial markets in Asia are mixed in Wednesday trading as artificial intelligence stocks bounce back.
After driving losses on Wall Street, the markets in South Korea, Japan, and Taiwan have rebounded after earlier losses other regional markets declined.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump says he concluded a big trade deal with the Philippines, without giving details
Trump heads to China for meetings with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin
Democrat Mary Peltola defeats Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska, giving Democrats a Senate seat
Democrat Raymond Smith defeats Republican Congressman Greg Murphy in tight North Carolina House race
Jensen Huang to answer closed-door questions before House committees in early December over chip smuggling
NVIDIA board rejects Jensen Huang's offer to return as CEO, says it won't reinstate him
Closing arguments end in Brooklyn trial of Huawei Technologies accused of criminal enterprise
Strong El Niño waves over 30 feet pound California coast, damaging Pacifica homes
Asian financial markets mixed as artificial intelligence stocks rebound after Wall Street losses
